issues.issue: The fallback chain sends undefined capitalized terms to the Policy and then the Indenture, but terms actually used in this Agreement — "Seller" in Section 3.02(a), "Collateral" in Section 2.01(j), "Rating Agencies" — are defined in none of the three. The interpretive rule therefore leaves operative terms without any assigned meaning.

"1119 Parties" is a closed list of six named entities with no provision for successors or replacements (e.g. a successor servicer or trustee), so the Section 2.05(o) no-affiliation representation is frozen to those six names. Expressio unius makes any later-appointed transaction party fall outside the term.

"Commission" is defined as the Securities and Exchange Commission while "SEC" is separately defined as the same agency, and the two terms are used in different operative provisions (2.02(e)(i) and 2.02(m) versus 2.05(i)). A court could be asked whether the two defined terms were meant to carry different content.

The definition points to "Section 2.02(c)(ill)", a garbled cross-reference; the Data Tape is in fact defined in Section 2.02(c)(iii)(A). The mechanical error leaves the source of the definition to be reconstructed.

The definition opens an enumeration with "(i)" and never supplies a "(ii)", indicating an omitted limb, and it is frozen to fiscal years ended November 30, 2004-2006. Section 2.01(h)'s reference to "the most recent Financial Statements" and 2.02(c)(i)'s ongoing annual statements cannot sit comfortably in that fixed definition.

"Holder" is said to take its meaning from the Policy, but the Policy defines "Owner" of the Insured Obligations and never defines "Holder". The term used throughout this Agreement (including the Policy definition in 1.01 and Section 2.02(c)) therefore has no assigned meaning in the instrument it points to.

"[T]he first January 31 to occur thereafter" does not say thereafter from what — the No Form 15D Notice or January 31, 2008 — so a notice given in late 2007 either extends the date by a year or by nothing at all. The extension mechanism can be read to be self-cancelling.

The definition cross-refers to "Section 2.03()", which is the Negative Covenants section and contains no such definition; "Insurer Financial Statements" is actually defined in Section 2.05(l). The broken cite leaves the defined term without a stated source.

The term is spelled "Tnsurer Information" and is cross-referenced to Section 3.04(a)(v), an indemnification provision, while the representation using "Insurer Information" is in Section 2.05(e). The mismatch between where the term is defined and where it does its work is a mechanical defect.

Limb (a)(ii), "the then applicable rate of interest on the Insured Notes", does not say which rate applies where the Insured Notes comprise two classes (A-1 and A-2) bearing different rates. The formula cannot be computed without choosing between them.

"Material Adverse Change" is expanded by "any material adverse change in the business, financial condition, results of operations or properties ... which might have such effect", so a mere possibility of impairment satisfies the test. The trigger word "might" has no boundary and this term controls covenants, defaults and reporting throughout Article II.

After enumerating the Prospectus, Prospectus Supplement and Free Writing Prospectus, the definition adds a catch-all for "any other offering document in respect of the Securities prepared by or on behalf of the Depositor that makes reference to the Policy". Whether marketing or investor materials outside the enumerated three fall within it is left open.

The catch-all limb captures only "each other document contemplated by any of the foregoing to which the Depositor, the Owner Trustee, the Master Servicer, the Servicer, the Indenture Trustee or the Trust is a party", omitting EMC/the Sponsor and the Insurer though EMC-side instruments (the Purchase Agreement, the Depositor Purchase Agreement, the Assignment Agreement) are enumerated. Expressio unius leaves EMC's other transaction documents outside the term on which nearly every covenant depends.

The enumerated list includes the "Certificate of Trust" and the "Administration Agreement", neither of which is defined in Article I or identified anywhere else in this Agreement. Their identity must be supplied from outside the instrument.

The definition turns on "any Mortgage Loan", a term this Agreement never defines and which sits against the recitals' and Article II's consistent use of "HELOCs" for the asset pool. Whether "Originators" reaches the originators of the HELOCs is therefore left to inference.

The Policy is defined as "issued by the Insurer in favor of the Indenture Trustee, for the benefit of the Holders", but the Financial Guaranty Insurance Policy No. CA03607A filed in the case names LaSalle Bank National Association, as Securities Administrator, as the Beneficiary and pays it, not the Indenture Trustee. Who holds and may claim under the Policy cannot be squared as between the two documents.

"Premium" is defined by three simultaneous references — payable "in accordance with this Insurance Agreement", "as 'Premium Amounts' pursuant to the Premium Letter" and "in accordance with the Indenture" — without saying which governs on a conflict. The circularity leaves the amount and timing of Premium indeterminate on the face of the definition.

The recitals define the "Purchase Agreement" and the "Servicing Agreement" as the same instrument — the Seller's Purchase, Warranties and Servicing Agreement dated October 18, 2004 as amended by Amendment Number One — differing only in the inclusion of the September 2006 term sheets. Yet Section 1.01's "Operative Documents" lists them as two separate documents, so the two defined terms overlap and cannot both be given independent effect.

"SEC" duplicates the separately defined "Commission", and the two are used in different provisions (2.05(i) and (l) versus 2.02(e) and (m)) of the same instrument. A court could be asked whether the drafters intended a distinction between the two labels.

"Servicer Information" is confined to information "contained under the heading 'The Servicer'" in the Offering Document, so servicer-related disclosure appearing under any other caption falls outside both the Section 2.04(e) representation and the Section 2.01(m) carve-out. The caption-based boundary is the whole of the definition.

"Transaction" is defined by open reference to everything "contemplated by the Operative Documents" plus everything "described in the Offering Document", with no boundary. Because "material adverse effect upon the Transaction" is the trigger in 2.01(a), (i), 2.02(e) and elsewhere, the vagueness is operative.

The rule that "include" and "including" mean "without limitation" pulls against the closed enumerations elsewhere, notably the "Operative Documents" definition and Section 2.03(d)'s list of successor roles, where the parties plainly intended finite lists. Whether the expansive rule overrides expressio unius in those provisions is left open.

The representation is made "as of the Closing Date" yet reads "is, or shall become, duly qualified" and "has obtained, or shall obtain, all necessary licenses", so nothing is actually represented to be true at closing and no deadline is fixed for becoming qualified. Whether this is a representation or an open-ended covenant is unclear from its own words.

Limb (ii) is qualified by breach that "reasonably could result in a Material Adverse Change" while limbs (i) and (iii) use "reasonably could be expected to result". The inconsistent standards within one subsection invite argument that a lower threshold applies to contractual defaults.

The first sentence covers only "Neither EMC nor the Depositor", omitting the Issuer even though the Section 2.01 chapeau has each of EMC, the Issuer and the Depositor representing as to itself. Whether the Issuer makes the no-contractual-default representation at all turns on that omission.

The closing sentence — each party "will not at any time in the future deny" that the Operative Documents are binding — is a perpetual forward promise embedded in a representation expressly made "as of the Closing Date". Whether it is a warranty, an estoppel or a covenant, and how it is breached, is not settled by the words used.

The contingent-liabilities sentence turns on liabilities that "have a material possibility of causing a Material Adverse Change", a standard found nowhere else in the Agreement and with no stated benchmark. "Material possibility" is a bare likelihood test that cannot be measured.

The Issuer represents it owns the Collateral "free and clear of all liens", which cannot be reconciled with Section 2.01(q)'s representation that on the Closing Date the Indenture Trustee "shall have a first perfected priority interest in the collateral" under the Indenture pledge. Both cannot be literally true at the same moment.

The defined term "Documents" sweeps in the Operative Documents plus all "other material information relating to the HELOCs, the operations ... or the financial condition" of the three parties "furnished to the Insurer in writing or in electronic form", with no time limit or identification of what was furnished. The boundary of the represented universe of information is undeterminable.

The closing sentence gives an unqualified warranty that "the information in the Data Tape with respect to each HELOC is true and correct as of the Cut-off Date", which sits against Section 2.02(n)'s repurchase machinery and Section 7 of the Depositor Purchase Agreement, where cure/repurchase/substitution is the "sole and exclusive remedy" for loan-level breaches. Whether the Insurer has a damages claim here or only the repurchase remedy is exactly what the two provisions leave open.

The proviso carves out "the Servicer Information or the Underwriter Information" and the sentence following speaks of "the Offered Notes", but neither "Underwriter Information" nor "Offered Notes" is defined in Article I or anywhere else in this Agreement. The scope of the disclosure representation turns on undefined terms.

This subsection imports every representation in every Operative Document and makes it directly to the Insurer "as if the same were set forth in full herein", which cannot be squared with Section 7 of the Depositor Purchase Agreement and Section 2.03 of the Sale and Servicing Agreement, where cure, repurchase or substitution is the "sole and exclusive remedy" for breach of those representations. Whether the Insurer thereby obtained a free-standing damages claim is the direct collision.

The subsection is captioned "Locations of Parties" but states only each party's jurisdiction of organization, saying nothing about location for filing or chief executive office purposes. The caption and the text describe different things, which matters given Section 2.02(f)'s financing statement covenant.

The representation is that the Indenture Trustee "shall have a first perfected priority interest in the collateral", using an uncapitalized "collateral" that is not a defined term here (contrast the capitalized "Collateral" in 2.01(j)). What property is covered, and what perfection steps are warranted, is not stated.

The compliance covenant is limited to "all cases in which failure to so comply or perform would result in a default thereunder", so the obligation to perform exists only where non-performance would itself be a default. The circular qualifier makes the scope of the covenant indeterminate.

The covenant requires each party, including the Servicer, to remain duly qualified and authorized "as described in subsections 2.01(a), (b) and (c) hereof", but those subsections are representations of EMC, the Issuer and the Depositor only; the Servicer's counterparts are Sections 2.04(a)-(c). The cross-reference cannot be applied to the Servicer as written.

The closing proviso allows website posting of "the information required to be furnished pursuant to Section 2.02(d)(iii)(B)", but Section 2.02(d) is the access-to-records covenant and has no clause (iii)(B); the servicing tape requirement is in Section 2.02(c)(iii)(B). The misdirected cross-reference leaves it unclear which reporting may be satisfied by website posting.

The trigger clause strings together "Once in each calendar year, or at any time following any ... Ratings Event, following the occurrence of any Default or Event of Default ..., at any time that the Overcollateralization Target Amount has not been reduced ..., and with respect to the Servicer, an Event of Servicer Termination has occurred", so it cannot be told whether these are alternative triggers or cumulative conditions. The scope of the Insurer's inspection right, and who bears its cost, turns on that reading.

Clause (i)(A) — a claim or proceeding "that (A) would be required to be disclosed to the Commission or its shareholders that relates to the HELOCs, the Transaction or its ability to perform" — is ungrammatical, leaving unclear whose shareholders are meant and whether the relatedness test qualifies (A) or the whole clause. The reporting trigger cannot be applied without repairing the sentence.

The further-assurances sentence obliges the parties, on the Insurer's reasonable request and within ten days, to execute "such amendments hereto and such further instruments and take such further action as may be reasonably necessary" — an open-ended duty to amend this Agreement itself. What amendment is "reasonably necessary to effectuate the intention" of the Operative Documents has no boundary.

This covenant directs the Securities Administrator to surrender the Policy on retirement of the Insured Notes, but Section 1.01 defines the Policy as "issued by the Insurer in favor of the Indenture Trustee". Who actually holds the Policy and can surrender it is left inconsistent as between the two provisions.

The subsection opens "It will not use, or distribute to any Person for use, any information relating to the Insurer" with no antecedent for "It", while the Section 2.02 chapeau names four covenantors (EMC, the Issuer, the Depositor and the Servicer). Which of them is bound by the disclosure restriction is not stated.

This makes the Insurer a third-party beneficiary of "all rights provided to the Insurer in the Operative Documents", which sits against Section 2.03 of the Sale and Servicing Agreement and Section 7 of the Depositor Purchase Agreement, whose sole-remedy clauses run only to the Issuing Entity, the Indenture Trustee and the Noteholders. Whether the Insurer's beneficiary status carries remedies those documents withhold is unresolved.

The covenant requires each covenantor to observe "(i) the obligation to hold annual meetings of its beneficial owners, shareholders or its board of directors", formalities that a Delaware statutory trust and a limited liability company are not required to observe. The qualifier "as applicable" leaves it undetermined which formalities are actually owed by which entity.

The delivery obligation extends to "an executed original copy of each document executed in connection with the Transaction", a category with no enumeration or boundary and broader than the defined "Operative Documents". What must be delivered within the 30 days is therefore uncertain.

This covenant obliges the Depositor to have the Issuer incorporate Insurer Financial Statements into every Form 10-D without any end date, whereas Section 2.05(i) gives the Insurer's consent to such incorporation only "through the Incorporation Termination Date". After that date the covenant requires what the Insurer has not consented to.

This subsection makes a mortgagor's TILA claim conclusive notice of breach, deems "[a]ny such breach ... material", and imposes repurchase plus a defence-and-indemnity obligation running to the Insurer; Section 7 of the Depositor Purchase Agreement requires a breach that "materially and adversely affects the value" and makes cure/repurchase/substitution the "sole and exclusive remedy", as does Section 2.03 of the Sale and Servicing Agreement. The two cannot both be given effect on materiality or on the availability of indemnity damages.

Receipt of notice of a claim "as a result of a violation or alleged violation" of the Truth-in-Lending Act is made to "conclusively constitute notice ... of a breach", so an unproven allegation by a mortgagor establishes a breach irrebuttably. Whether "alleged violation" was meant to fix liability without adjudication of the underlying claim is the ambiguity.

The covenant is framed in terms of "All Mortgage Loans", a term this Agreement never defines, while the asset pool is defined in the recitals as the HELOCs and master servicing is governed by the Sale and Servicing Agreement rather than the Servicing Agreement named here. What loans must be serviced under which agreement is left unresolved by the sentence's own words.

Notice must be given "promptly prior to the date of consummation of such action or failure to act", which cannot sensibly be applied to a failure to act, and the covenant itself bites on anything that "may result" in a Material Adverse Change. Both the trigger and the timing are indeterminate on the face of the paragraph.

The consent requirement excepts "any amendment to the Offering Document required by law", presupposing that the Offering Document is one of the Operative Documents to which the covenant applies, but the Section 1.01 definition of "Operative Documents" does not include it. The carve-out and the defined term cannot both be given their natural effect.

The merger prohibition is subject to the exception "except as provided in the Operative Documents or as permitted hereby", yet nothing in this Agreement permits any consolidation, merger or asset transfer. The scope of the exception must be supplied from outside the sentence.

The restriction binds only "EMC, the Issuer and the Depositor", dropping the Servicer that the Section 2.03 chapeau brings within the negative covenants, and lists only Paying Agent, Custodian, Indenture Trustee and Owner Trustee, omitting the Master Servicer and Securities Administrator. Expressio unius leaves successor appointments to those omitted roles unrestricted.

The covenant turns entirely on "its status as a bankruptcy remote entity", a term neither defined in Article I nor tied to any enumerated separateness criteria. What conduct causes a failure to maintain that status cannot be determined from the provision.

The Servicer is represented to be organized "under the laws of the jurisdiction of its incorporation" without naming that jurisdiction, unlike Section 2.01(a), which names Delaware for each of EMC, the Depositor and the Issuer. The representation is self-referential and warrants nothing identifiable.

The Servicer's disclosure representation is confined to the "Servicer Information", which Section 1.01 limits to text "under the heading 'The Servicer'" in the Offering Document. Servicer-related disclosure appearing under any other heading is covered by no representation of the Servicer at all.

The chapeau treats everything in Section 2.05 as a representation made as of the Closing Date "and, in the case of Section 2.05(g) below, covenants during the term", yet Sections 2.05(i), (k), (m) and (n) plainly impose continuing obligations running to the Incorporation Termination Date. Whether those subsections are covenants at all cannot be squared with the chapeau's single carve-out for (g).

The representation is expressly cut down to "such limited scope of disclosure" as would be required were the Insurer not the registrant, a self-defining limit with no ascertainable content. What the Insurer actually warrants about the Insurer Information depends on that undefined boundary.

The confidentiality undertaking is excepted where disclosure is "requested by appropriate governmental authorities" or "as necessary to preserve its rights or security under or to enforce the Operative Documents" — exceptions requiring no compulsion and defined by the Insurer's own judgment. The carve-outs are broad enough to be argued to swallow the covenant.

The Insurer's compliance representation is tested by whether a violation "could result in a Material Adverse Change with respect to the Insurer", but Section 1.01 defines that term by reference to ability to perform "under any of the Operative Documents", and the Policy is not among the Operative Documents listed there. The Insurer's principal obligation therefore falls outside the very test the provision uses.

The Insurer need only "use commercially reasonable efforts" to obtain its accountants' consent letter, with no benchmark and no consequence stated if the letter is not obtained. The undefined effort standard governs the Depositor's ability to make its Regulation AB filings.

The representation is framed by reference to reports required "pursuant to Section 13(a) or 15(d) of the Exchange Act", a term not defined in Article I, which defines only "Securities Exchange Act". The same sentence then reverts to "the Securities Exchange Act", leaving the two labels to be reconciled.

The trigger includes "if the representation in Section 2.05(i) is no longer true", but Section 2.05(i) is the Insurer's consent to incorporation by reference and contains no representation; the representation is in Section 2.05(j), which itself points forward to this subsection. The misdirected cross-reference makes the condition for furnishing financial statements uncertain.

This subsection is where "Insurer Financial Statements" is actually defined, yet Section 1.01 states the term "has the meaning assigned to such term in Section 2.03() below". The definition and its stated source cannot be reconciled.

The Insurer must disclose affiliations only "to the extent actually known and material", with no inquiry duty and no materiality benchmark, and its deadline runs from a filing date the Depositor merely "has stated" in its own certificate. Both the content and the timing of the obligation are set by undefined standards.

The Insurer agrees to comply with "all reasonable requests" for information "necessary for the Depositor to comply with Item 1114", without identifying Item 1114 of Regulation AB or bounding what information is necessary. The obligation's scope rests entirely on the undefined word "reasonable".

The no-affiliation representation ends with the garbled qualifier "without regard to affiliations by common control-with the Insurer", which either excludes common-control affiliates from the representation or does the opposite. That carve-out determines the entire content of the representation.

The Section 3.01 chapeau has the Insurer agreeing "to issue the Policy on the Closing Date subject to satisfaction of the conditions precedent", while the recitals state that "the Insurer has issued the Policy" and the Policy itself is dated the same day. Whether the Policy was conditional on these deliveries or already unconditionally issued is a recital-versus-operative conflict.

The condition is satisfied only by documents "in form and substance reasonably satisfactory to the Insurer", a purely subjective standard with no objective referent. What suffices is measured only by the Insurer's own view.

The condition covers representations "set forth or incorporated by reference in this Insurance Agreement", which by Section 2.01(n) means every representation in every Operative Document, without any materiality qualifier. How far the incorporation reaches for purposes of this closing condition is not stated here.

The condition calls for opinions "addressed to any of Moody's, S&P, the Indenture Trustee, the Owner Trustee, EMC, the Issuer, the Depositor and the Underwriter" and, in the same sentence, "addressed to the Insurer". Whether an opinion addressed only to another party satisfies the condition cannot be told from the text.

The condition fails if any proceeding "shall be pending or threatened", with no knowledge qualifier, no materiality threshold and no statement of who must perceive the threat. Any asserted threat of suit would literally defeat the condition.

The condition turns on the Underwriter's obligation "to purchase the Offered Notes", a term not defined in Article I or anywhere in this Agreement, though "Notes" and "Insured Notes" are both defined. Which classes the condition covers is left open.

The ratings condition requires that "the Notes that are rated, when issued, will be rated 'AAA' by S&P and 'Aaa' by Moody's", without identifying which classes are the rated Notes; the Class B Notes plainly would not carry those ratings. The self-selecting phrase "the Notes that are rated" makes the condition circular.

The condition is that "[n]o Default or Event of Default shall have occurred", omitting the "and is continuing" qualifier that Section 2.01(f) attaches to the identical representation. A cured Default would fail this condition but not that representation.

The condition is met only if the Insurer and its counsel "shall have reasonably determined" that all documents "conform to the terms" of five separate instruments, without saying what non-conformity matters. Both the standard of conformity and the reasonableness of the determination are unbounded.

The condition requires "evidence satisfactory to it" of delivery and endorsement, with satisfaction left wholly to the Insurer and no form of evidence specified. What discharges the condition is not ascertainable from the text.

Periodic rating agency fees are billed to "the Seller", a capitalized term that is defined nowhere in this Agreement, in the Policy or in the parties list, which uses "Sponsor", "Depositor" and "Issuer"; "Rating Agencies" is likewise undefined here. Who must pay the ongoing fees cannot be determined from the subsection.

The obligation is to pay fees "incurred by the Insurer in connection with the issuance of the Policy amounts and as described in the Premium Letter", a sentence whose words do not parse and which may mean either fees in the amounts described in the Premium Letter or fees of the kinds described there. The measure of what EMC owes at closing turns on the broken phrase.

The Premium is stated to be "fully earned by the Insurer as of the date of issuance" and nonrefundable, yet "payable in periodic installments of Premium Amounts as provided in the Premium Letter" and "in accordance with ... Section 3.02 of the Indenture". Whether the whole earned Premium becomes payable on early termination or redemption, or only installment by installment through the Indenture waterfall, is unresolved.

Reimbursement is expressed as arising "[a]s and when due in accordance with and from the funds specified in Section 3.02(a) of the Indenture", which can be read to confine the Insurer's reimbursement right to the Indenture waterfall, against Section 3.02(c) and the Article III indemnity obligations that make EMC directly liable to the Insurer. Whether reimbursement is a general obligation or a limited-recourse claim on trust funds is the collision.
